# Independent PDN3 conversion fixtures

The two tiny `.pdn` files were produced by the independent
[`PdnDocumentCodec.js`](https://github.com/LabyStudio/paintdotjs/blob/6fe29faa80fd3a51e84fd97ab8d7ba03b9e637a7/js/src/io/PdnDocumentCodec.js)
writer, pinned at PaintDotJS commit
`6fe29faa80fd3a51e84fd97ab8d7ba03b9e637a7`. Its source states that the
[`assets/pdn/templates`](https://github.com/LabyStudio/paintdotjs/tree/6fe29faa80fd3a51e84fd97ab8d7ba03b9e637a7/assets/pdn/templates)
graphs were generated by Paint.NET 5.1.12. We used its 1/2-layer graph templates
through the writer's own dimension/property patching, then supplied original
3 x 2 RGBA test pixels through its canvas input interface. Node's built-in
`CompressionStream("gzip")` performed the writer's compression.

These are independent-writer conversion fixtures, not untouched documents saved
by Microsoft Paint.NET in our environment. They prove this observed graph/pixel
path, not native application fidelity or a PaintCraft writer. The header claims
`5.112.9563.32325`; the graph's savedWith object contains zeros. The decoder retains
those independent untrusted claims without assuming that they must agree.

Both fixtures contain original arithmetic pixel patterns, including RGB under
zero alpha, Unicode layer names, distinct visibility/opacity and a background-role
flag. The two-layer fixture sets the writer's chunk size to 8 so it contains
three gzip chunks per layer. The accompanying JSON files record exact source
commit, original template hashes, graph/pixel boundary, chunk size, file SHA-256,
expected properties and complete RGBA hashes/hex. Tests reorder chunk records
without changing indexes to exercise the original PDN out-of-order chunk rule.

No original application art, toolbar icons, embedded UI resources, logo or GPC
code is included. Only generated serialization graphs and original test pixels
are present. The upstream [license](LICENSE-paintdotjs.txt) and
[attribution notice](NOTICE-paintdotjs.md) are retained in full, including their
historical resource exceptions. PaintCraft's decoder implementation is independent
Rust using the public inert record/framing definitions; it does not host .NET,
BinaryFormatter, JavaScript or Paint.NET DLLs.

The deferred framing is independently documented by the original historical
[`MemoryBlock.cs`](https://github.com/rivy/OpenPDN/blob/cca476b0df2a2f70996e6b9486ec45327631568c/src/Core/MemoryBlock.cs)
and [`DeferredFormatter.cs`](https://github.com/rivy/OpenPDN/blob/cca476b0df2a2f70996e6b9486ec45327631568c/src/Base/DeferredFormatter.cs).
NRBF record definitions come from Microsoft's
[MS-NRBF](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-nrbf/5acd9dc4-1439-433a-8d53-eb2922a142d8).
No heuristic scan for plausible pixel headers is used: the parser returns the
exact MessageEnd boundary and reconstructs the typed buffer identities first.
